title: Finite integral scalar tensor reindexing square
statement: Fix a prime l, schemes X,Y with l invertible in their residue fields, an isomorphism g:X→Y, native realizations R,S with tensor data A,C, a function-normalized ring reindexing B, and one finite coefficient index E. Let NX,NY be their finite normalizations, V an integral scalar reindexing and W its ordinary tensor reindexing. Use the maps of [def-sf-adic-integral-tensor-coordinates]. For integral constructible K,L on Y, write P for integral pullback, TY for completed integral tensor, EX,EY for ordinary derived scalar extension, and F for ordinary derived reindexing. Then F(finiteIntegralTensorMap NY K L) followed by finiteIntegralPullMap V (TY(K,L)) and EX(canonicalIntegralPullbackTensor K L) equals W.tensor.hom at (EY K,EY L), followed by A.closed.tensor applied to the two finiteIntegralPullMap components and finiteIntegralTensorMap NX (PK) (PL). No common-stage realization comparison or common-stage tensorator occurs.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15, printed pp. 61-62; Hemo--Richarz--Scholbach, Lemma 7.9.
source.note: The explicit postcomposition is the cancellation stage in the fixed-field representative calculation.

proof.text: Compare the two normalized ordinary tensor presentations with the fixed ambient tensor by fully faithful restriction to good pairs. Factor finiteIntegralTensorMap into finiteAmbientScalarTensor.inv followed by scalar extension of tensorPresentationCompletion.

Apply the ordinary scalar tensor square and the independent integral quotient-completion square. Naturality of V.derived moves the completion map past the scalar reindexing. Functoriality applies EX to the integral square; the ordinary square then replaces the three ordinary factors. Naturality of finiteAmbientScalarTensor.inv moves the two complete-input identifications to the native tensor, where functoriality combines them with V.derived. This is the original equation.

proof_origin.note: Complete Lean categorical pasting of separate ordinary scalar and integral completion squares. The presentation comparison is constructed by fully faithful restriction, without a new existence hole.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_integral_tensor_reindexing
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso g]
    (R : LocallyFiniteAdicRealization.Realization l X)
    (S : LocallyFiniteAdicRealization.Realization l Y)
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)]
    [∀ y : Y, Invertible (l : Y.residueField y)]
    (A : At l X R) (C : At l Y S) (B : RingReindex l X g R S)
    (E : AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Index l (PadicAlgCl l))
    (NX : FiniteNormalization l X R A E) (NY : FiniteNormalization l Y S C E)
    (V : IntegralReindex l X g B E) (W : ReindexTensor l X g A C B)
    (K L : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l
      (AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Coefficient.{u} l (PadicAlgCl l) E) Y) :
    let P := constructibleIntegralPullback l
      (AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Coefficient.{u} l (PadicAlgCl l) E) g
    let TY := constructibleIntegralTensor l
      (AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Coefficient.{u} l (PadicAlgCl l) E) Y
    let EX := pbcDerivedExtend (coefficientMap l X R E)
    let EY := pbcDerivedExtend (coefficientMap l Y S E)
    let F := derivedPull l X g B
    F.map (finiteIntegralTensorMap l Y S C E NY K L) ≫
        finiteIntegralPullMap l g R S B E V (TY.obj (K, L)) ≫
        EX.map (canonicalIntegralPullbackTensor l
          (AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Coefficient.{u} l (PadicAlgCl l) E) g K L).hom.hom =
      W.tensor.hom.app (EY.obj K.obj, EY.obj L.obj) ≫
        A.closed.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom
          (finiteIntegralPullMap l g R S B E V K)
          (finiteIntegralPullMap l g R S B E V L)) ≫
        finiteIntegralTensorMap l X R A E NX (P.obj K) (P.obj L)
